قبل بدء الدرس

مرحبا بك في حصة تعلم اللغة الانجليزية

استعد لدرس ممتع عن السفر والمطار. الهدف هو التحدث بثقة واستخدام جمل قصيرة وواضحة.

🎙️

تحقق من صوتك

تأكد أن الميكروفون يعمل بوضوح.

📷

شغّل الكاميرا

اجلس في مكان هادئ وإضاءة جيدة.

📶

اتصال مستقر

اختبر الإنترنت قبل بدء الحصة.

📝

جهّز أدواتك

ورقة وقلم، واستعد للتحدث.

قبل أن نبدأ

هل تستطيع التحدث عن رحلتك بالإنجليزية؟

بعد ٢٥ دقيقة، ستفعلها بثقة!

اليوم نتعلم كلمات السفر، ثم نجري محادثة حقيقية في المطار — خطوة بخطوة، دون خوف.

Objective · who is who at check-in
New words · people

You are the passenger. The agent helps you.

passengerPASS-en-ger · a person who travels on a plane
agentAY-jent · the person who helps you at the counter

New word
Gate

The place where you get on the plane.

Objective · dialogue part 1: check-in & passport
Real conversation · Part 1 of 2

At the check-in counter.

Traveler
Good morning! I’d like to check in, please.
Agent
Good morning! May I have your passport?
Traveler
Sure, here you are.

Practice: you are the traveler — say all the traveler lines!

Objective · dialogue part 2: seats & boarding pass
Real conversation · Part 2 of 2

Seats and the boarding pass.

Traveler
Can I have a window seat, please?
Agent
I’m sorry, no window seats. Is an aisle seat OK?
Traveler
Yes, that’s fine. Thank you!
Agent
Here’s your boarding pass. Gate B7. Have a nice flight!

Objective · useful travel words

More words for your trip — look, listen and say 👂

carry-on bagCARE-ee-on · /ˈkæri ɒn bæɡ/

A small bag you take on the plane.

My carry-on bag is under the seat.

checked luggageCHECKED LUG-gage · /tʃekt ˈlʌɡɪdʒ/

Big bags you give at check-in.

My checked luggage is 20 kilos.

visaVEE-za · /ˈviːzə/

A stamp that lets you enter a country.

You need a visa for this trip.

first classFIRST CLASS · /fɜːst klɑːs/

The best, biggest seats on the plane.

First class has big seats.

business classBUSI-ness class · /ˈbɪznəs klɑːs/

Big, comfy seats for work trips.

Business class is very comfy.

New words

New expressions

  • May I have your passport?
  • Sure, here you are.
  • Can I have a window seat, please?
  • I’m sorry, no window seats.
  • Is an aisle seat OK?
  • Here’s your boarding pass. Gate B7.
  • Have a nice flight!
  • I like a window seat.
  • I’m going to ___ by ___.
  • Where are you flying today?

Reference · visible for teacher
CEFR reference

CEFR levels and key abilities

C2Understands virtually everything with ease; summarizes and expresses ideas precisely.
C1Understands complex texts and implicit meaning; communicates flexibly and effectively.
B2Understands main ideas of complex texts; communicates fluently and interacts naturally.
B1Understands familiar topics; handles many situations and describes experiences.
A2Understands common expressions and simple information; communicates in routine tasks.
A1Understands basic phrases; introduces oneself and answers simple questions slowly.
Lesson fit: this travel lesson mainly targets A1+ speaking functions.
